teaching.note: ADVISORY ONLY: written by a language model from one session's journal. It cannot change configuration, risk limits, sizing or gates, and it promotes nothing; a proposed change is a hypothesis for a pre-registered study.
teaching.summary: One BANKNIFTY va_reversion bear put spread on a balance day hit its POC target for +0.55R, capturing 94% of best open profit. Range_sell was found and rejected roughly 190 times on EV hovering near zero; later reads showed slightly positive EV still refused. Late engine start (vol shadow empty) and frozen closing bars limit what can be learned. One trade is thin evidence.

lessons.claim: The va_reversion short from a failed VAH probe (54,167.60) to POC 54,065.54 was well formed and well managed: target hit in 18 bars, 94% of best open profit kept, worst heat 0.04R.
lessons.why: The thesis matched the day type the desk had already labelled balance since 10:24. A defined-risk spread with a level-based exit took the rotation without giving profit back.
lessons.uncertainty: A single trade on one balance day. Shallow heat and a fast fill could be luck. After exit, price rose back toward 54,147, so the timing was favourable.

lessons.claim: Range_sell was re-evaluated almost every minute and rejected with EV oscillating between about ₹-240 and ₹+30 per lot. These near-duplicate rejections add noise, not information.
lessons.why: About 190 decision rows share one reason. Minute-to-minute EV swings of ₹100–200 suggest quote noise in the iron_fly pricing rather than a real change in edge.
lessons.uncertainty: The swings may reflect genuine bid/ask changes. Without the bars, quote noise cannot be separated from signal.
lessons.hypothesis: The iron_fly EV estimate's minute-to-minute variance is dominated by spread/quote noise, not by underlying movement.
lessons.confirm_if: Across sessions, the absolute change in EV between consecutive minutes correlates weakly (|r|<0.2) with the absolute change in underlying price over the same minute.
lessons.refute_if: The EV changes track underlying moves or implied-vol changes with |r|>0.5.

lessons.claim: From 12:06 to 13:15 the BANKNIFTY iron_fly read positive EV (₹+28 to +167/lot) on a balance day that kept rotating around 54,050–54,070, yet no range_sell opened.
lessons.why: The balance-day thesis paid on the directional trade. The neutral structure the desk kept finding was marginally positive but sat below the floor, so the floor, not the setup, decided.
lessons.uncertainty: Positive EV of +0.03R is within model error. The direction model's AUC of 0.537 is barely informative. Hypothetical P&L is unknown, and the frozen bars affect late-session marking.
lessons.hypothesis: Range_sell setups rejected with EV between 0 and the floor would, on balance days, have realised positive P&L net of costs.
lessons.confirm_if: A shadow replay of rejected range_sell candidates with EV>0 on balance-labelled days shows mean realised R >0 across at least 20 sessions.
lessons.refute_if: The same replay shows mean realised R ≤0, or a confidence interval spanning zero after 20 sessions.

lessons.claim: The engine reached its opening read only at 12:22, so the volatility shadow recorded nothing for either index today.
lessons.why: Losing the vol shadow on a session that produced the only trade removes the comparison data that the plan study (15 of 28 sessions) needs. Late starts slow accumulation of a point-in-time record.
lessons.uncertainty: The cause of the late start is not recorded. It may be a one-off infrastructure issue.

lessons.claim: The 09:33 BANKNIFTY bearish read (conv 0.49) armed an ORB sell that never triggered, and price then rallied to about 54,254 by 10:05. Standing aside on breaking news around 09:47 coincided with that reversal.
lessons.why: An untriggered ORB avoided a short into a rally. Whether this came from the gate's design or from luck cannot be told from one day.
lessons.uncertainty: The news-stand-aside effect cannot be isolated, and the news headline (gold/Fed) was not BANKNIFTY-specific.

teaching.summary: One trade: a NIFTY ORB long call opened at 10:06, a minute after an ORB rejection at EV ₹-43/lot. It never made more than 0.06R and was exited on invalidation at -0.59R. The other 44 distinct decisions were EV-floor rejections. Range_sell iron_flies showed P(profit) 0% throughout. Chain outages and a repeat 12:22 late start limit what this session can teach.

lessons.claim: The ORB entry chased an extended break. The trigger close of 22,788.95 was 42 pts above the OR high (22,746.40) and +1.7σ above VWAP. The invalidation sat 60 pts below. Best open profit was only 0.06R before invalidation.
lessons.why: Entering far from the breakout level means a normal retest reaches the invalidation. The trade had almost no favourable excursion, which suggests the move was already spent at entry.
lessons.uncertainty: One trade. The BANKNIFTY sell-off at 11:15 may have been a market-wide reversal that would have hit any long. The extension threshold is a guess.
lessons.hypothesis: ORB entries whose trigger close is above +1.5σ VWAP distance have lower max favourable excursion than ORB entries below that distance.
lessons.confirm_if: Over at least 20 recorded ORB triggers, median best open profit (R) for those at ≥1.5σ is below that for those at <1.5σ, with stop-outs more frequent.
lessons.refute_if: Median MFE and stop-out rates are similar, or better for extended entries.

lessons.claim: ORB NIFTY was rejected at 10:05 (EV ₹-43/lot, P(profit) 45%), then entered at 10:06 with 6 units. The journal does not record the EV that cleared the floor one minute later.
lessons.why: A flip from below the floor to a full-size entry within one bar suggests EV is computed near zero and is noisy. Whether 6 units was justified cannot be checked from these rows.
lessons.uncertainty: The accepted decision row is not in the journal. The EV at entry may have been comfortably positive.
lessons.hypothesis: Entries taken within 2 minutes of a same-setup EV rejection perform worse than entries with no recent rejection.
lessons.confirm_if: Across sessions, mean R of entries preceded by a same-setup rejection in the prior 2 minutes is lower than the mean R of other entries.
lessons.refute_if: Mean R is equal or higher for entries preceded by a recent rejection.

lessons.claim: The underlying-based invalidation exit worked as designed. The long call was cut at 22,723.10 through 22,728.98, for -0.59R with worst heat 0.64R, rather than being held toward full premium loss. NIFTY then printed 22,696.75 a minute later.
lessons.why: The exit followed the stated thesis level. Price kept falling right after, so holding would likely have deepened the loss.
lessons.uncertainty: NIFTY later recovered to about 22,760 by 10:40, so on another path the exit would have been a whipsaw. This is one instance.

lessons.claim: Every range_sell iron_fly rejection, from 11:11 to 13:04 on both indices, reported P(profit) 0% with EV pinned near -0.04R. That is implausible for a short iron fly in a balance regime.
lessons.why: A constant 0% profit probability across 20+ evaluations points to a pricing or model fault, not to market information. That makes the range_sell rejections uninformative.
lessons.uncertainty: It could be a deliberate cost model where fees always exceed premium at this size. The full structure details are truncated.
lessons.hypothesis: The iron_fly P(profit) calculation returns 0% regardless of strikes and premium.
lessons.confirm_if: Recomputing recorded iron_fly quotes offline gives P(profit) well above 0% for the same inputs.
lessons.refute_if: The offline recomputation also gives about 0% because costs exceed the credit.

lessons.claim: From 14:05 to 14:19, BANKNIFTY trend_break long_put EV swung between ₹-237 and ₹+182/lot across 12 evaluations. These were priced while the Kotak chain was down and NSE fallback data was in use.
lessons.why: Large minute-to-minute EV swings on fallback quotes suggest the floor comparison was dominated by quote noise, so these rejections tell us little about the setup.
lessons.uncertainty: The swings may reflect real premium moves. Entries were blocked by the chain rule anyway, so the cost here was nil.
lessons.hypothesis: EV dispersion per setup-minute is larger when pricing comes from the fallback chain than from the primary chain.
lessons.confirm_if: The standard deviation of consecutive-minute EV changes is clearly higher on fallback-flagged periods across sessions.
lessons.refute_if: The dispersion is similar on primary and fallback pricing.

lessons.claim: The volatility shadow again first reached the opening read at 12:22, the same timestamp as the prior session. Nothing was recorded for either index, and bars froze from 15:16 to 15:27.
lessons.why: A repeating identical late-start time looks systematic, not random. Each lost day delays the 28-session real data requirement in the plan study.
lessons.uncertainty: A two-day match could be coincidence. The cause is not in the journal.

teaching.summary: One NIFTY vwap_trend long put lost -0.62R on a time exit. It was entered at 10:06, a minute after the same setup was rejected on EV. It peaked at +0.84R open profit, then gave it all back as a crude-oil headline reversed. Range_sell rejections again showed implausible P(profit) values. Data and infrastructure warnings make the evening's records less reliable.

lessons.claim: The trade reached 0.84R of open profit and still closed at -0.62R on a 60-minute time exit. That is a 1.46R swing. Exit price 22,600.85 was still below the 22,607.64 invalidation, so neither a stop nor a target ever acted.
lessons.why: The structure had no rule that locks in open profit, and the time stop fired near the worst point of a reversal.
lessons.uncertainty: One trade only. Best open profit may be measured on option marks with wide spreads. A profit lock could also cut winners on other days.
lessons.hypothesis: On past vwap_trend trades whose open profit reached at least 0.75R, a simulated rule that exits at breakeven after reaching 0.75R raises the average R compared with the actual exits.
lessons.confirm_if: Across at least 20 recorded trades that reached 0.75R, the simulated average R beats the actual average R by at least 0.1R.
lessons.refute_if: The simulated average R is equal to or worse than the actual, or fewer than 20 qualifying trades exist.

lessons.claim: vwap_trend NIFTY was rejected at 10:05 with EV ₹+109/lot (+0.04R), then entered at 10:06 with 5 units. The journal does not record the EV that cleared the floor. The same pattern was flagged on 10-27.
lessons.why: An EV one minute below the floor turning into a 5-unit entry suggests the gate can flip on tiny changes in inputs. It leaves the entry's edge unauditable.
lessons.uncertainty: The 10:06 bar may truly have changed the inputs, for example the trigger completing. A missing log row is not proof of a bad entry.
lessons.hypothesis: Entries made within 2 minutes of a below-floor rejection of the same setup have a lower average R than other entries.
lessons.confirm_if: Over at least 30 entries, those preceded by a same-setup rejection within 2 minutes average at least 0.2R worse.
lessons.refute_if: The gap is under 0.1R, or reverses in sign.

lessons.claim: The entry came after a Brent-$115 headline (around 09:38) and before a 'crude falls on diplomacy' headline (around 10:48). The loss followed that second headline. The trend thesis was effectively a bet that the oil-shock move would continue.
lessons.why: News stand-asides covered the minutes right after each headline. The open position, though, carried exposure to headline reversal, which the thesis did not name.
lessons.uncertainty: The sample of reads may hide the exact timing. The reversal may have been ordinary mean reversion, not news-driven.

lessons.claim: The range_sell iron_fly was re-evaluated almost every minute from 11:30 to 12:17. EV stayed near -0.03R while P(profit) slid from 46% to 19%. That pairing is implausible for a short iron fly and repeats the 10-27 anomaly.
lessons.why: If P(profit) falls that far, EV should worsen sharply. The two numbers may come from inconsistent models or stale chain data. The kotak chain was down and the NSE fallback was in use.
lessons.uncertainty: Decay near midday could legitimately change the shape of the payoff. The fallback data might explain it all.
lessons.hypothesis: Iron_fly P(profit) and EV become inconsistent when chain data comes from the fallback source.
lessons.confirm_if: The correlation between P(profit) and EV across iron_fly evaluations is at least 0.3 lower on fallback-data minutes than on primary-data minutes.
lessons.refute_if: The correlation is similar on both sources.

lessons.claim: Standing aside on the BANKNIFTY vwap_trend and ORB rejections (10:20–10:25, EV near ₹0/lot) was correct. BANKNIFTY moved from 53,737 to about 54,000 by 11:05, where a long put would have lost.
lessons.why: The EV floor filtered out a short on an index that rotated up. P(up) 0.45 came from a weak direction model (AUC 0.532).
lessons.uncertainty: Judged by hindsight on one move. The filter's value needs many sessions to show.

lessons.claim: The vol-shadow warnings say the engine first reached the opening read at 12:22. Yet reads and decisions exist from 09:16. The same 12:22 text appeared on 10-26, which suggests a stale or buggy warning rather than a real late start.
lessons.why: Unreliable warnings reduce trust in the grading and data-quality records. The 51s slow step and the futures failure add to that.
lessons.uncertainty: The vol shadow may use a separate process that truly started late.

teaching.summary: Bullish trend day; four long calls netted about +1.2R. The best trade (083c, +0.82R) was held to square-off. The NIFTY flag breakout gave back most of a 1.27R open profit on a time exit. Entries keep following minute-old EV rejections without logging the EV that cleared the floor. The iron_fly P(profit) 0% readings recur. Data warnings (chain down, frozen bars, late vol shadow) limit trust.

lessons.claim: NIFTY trend_break 0002 reached 1.27R open profit, near the 22,905 target path (22,870.90 at 10:31). It exited at 22,828 on a 'no progress' time exit, keeping only 22%. This is the second straight session where a time exit gave back about 1R.
lessons.why: The time exit measures progress at the exit time, not from peak open profit. Once a trade has run, it surrenders the gain instead of protecting it.
lessons.uncertainty: Two sessions only. The peak may have been one brief spike that no rule could have captured. A tighter rule might cut trade 083c's run.
lessons.hypothesis: On trades that reach at least 1.0R open profit, a peak-anchored exit would retain more R than the 45-60 min no-progress exit.
lessons.confirm_if: Replayed on recorded bars across 20+ sessions, the peak-anchored variant's mean captured R exceeds the time exit's, without lowering 083c-type trades by more.
lessons.refute_if: Replay shows equal or lower mean captured R, or most ≥1R peaks reverse within one bar.

lessons.claim: All three trend_break entries followed rejections only minutes earlier with EV near zero. NIFTY: 10:17 at +0.04R, entered 10:20. BANKNIFTY: 10:28-10:32 at -0.01 to +0.01R, entered 10:33. BANKNIFTY again: 14:00, entered 14:05. The EV that cleared the floor is never logged.
lessons.why: Without the entry EV, nobody can tell whether the gate passed real edge or noise. Outcomes were mixed: +0.28R, -0.22R, +0.82R.
lessons.uncertainty: The entry EV may be stored elsewhere. Three trades is far too few to judge whether marginal-EV entries pay.
lessons.hypothesis: Entries whose preceding rejection showed |EV| < 0.05R earn no better mean R than zero after costs.
lessons.confirm_if: Over 30+ such entries with logged entry EV, mean realized R is within ±0.05R of zero or below.
lessons.refute_if: Mean realized R is significantly above 0.1R.

lessons.claim: BANKNIFTY trend_break 0003 entered with price 54,632.75, +2.0σ above VWAP and 33 pts past the trigger close. Best open profit was 0.07R against heat of 0.35R.
lessons.why: This was the second BANKNIFTY long within minutes of the ORB exit, bought late in an extended move. The 27 Oct ORB showed the same chase pattern.
lessons.uncertainty: One trade. The loss came from time decay and a pullback on a still-bullish day; a +2σ fill may not be a reliable predictor.
lessons.hypothesis: Breakout entries filled more than 1.8σ above VWAP have lower mean R than those filled below 1.8σ.
lessons.confirm_if: Across 40+ breakout entries, the >1.8σ bucket shows a lower mean R and a lower best-open-profit/heat ratio.
lessons.refute_if: There is no difference in mean R between the buckets.

lessons.claim: Trade 083c was held through the afternoon to the 15:15 square-off for +0.82R, grade A. The extension came after more than two hours of near-zero-EV rejections in a well-defined trend. Its invalidation at 22,867.62 was never hit.
lessons.why: Patience through the midday rejections (745-775) avoided low-EV chop. The trade then rode the bull tape to the end of the session.
lessons.uncertainty: The 15:15-15:28 bar freeze may affect the exit mark. One winning trade on a trend day proves little.

lessons.claim: The range_sell iron_fly showed P(profit) 0% at 13:19-13:21 and jumped back to 31% a minute later, with EV steady at about -0.03R. This repeats the 26-28 Oct pattern.
lessons.why: An iron_fly cannot have 0% profit probability while its EV stays near -0.03R. The pricing model looks inconsistent, so these rejections are noise, not information.
lessons.uncertainty: The P(profit) field may use a different horizon or include costs. This could be a display bug rather than a model bug.
lessons.hypothesis: Iron_fly P(profit) is inconsistent with its own EV and payoff distribution.
lessons.confirm_if: Recomputing P(profit) from the logged payoff and the distribution the EV uses gives values differing by more than 20 points on these rows.
lessons.refute_if: Recomputation reproduces about 0% under a documented, consistent definition.

lessons.claim: The data plumbing was unreliable. Kotak chain was down for BANKNIFTY (11:08) and NIFTY (12:00), entries were skipped, and the NIFTY futures snapshot failed. The vol shadow reports a late start at 12:22 although reads begin at 09:16. Bars froze from 15:15, the square-off minute.
lessons.why: Gating and grading depend on these feeds. The 12:22 late start repeats 26 Oct verbatim and contradicts the 09:16 thoughts.
lessons.uncertainty: The vol shadow may define its 'opening read' differently from the analyst loop. The freeze may not have touched the fills.

teaching.summary: Three long-call entries, all losers (-0.74R, -0.07R, -0.20R). Each was entered one minute after the same setup was rejected for EV below the floor, and the journal does not record the EV that let it through. The BANKNIFTY entry came one minute after a warning that BANKNIFTY entries were blocked. The ORB invalidation sat close to entry, and NIFTY later rallied about 145 pts past its exit. One session, so all of this is thin.

lessons.claim: BANKNIFTY trend_break opened at 12:02 one minute after event:843 said no new BANKNIFTY entries while the kotak chain was down. The journal does not show the chain recovering.
lessons.why: Either the entry gate was bypassed, or the chain recovered without a logged event. Both are control gaps worth auditing before trusting BANKNIFTY fills priced off the NSE fallback.
lessons.uncertainty: The chain may have recovered at 12:01–12:02 with no recovery event logged. The warning may cover only some entry paths.
lessons.hypothesis: Some entries are opened while a 'kotak chain down' warning for that index is still active.
lessons.confirm_if: Across sessions, entries exist after a chain-down WARN with no intervening chain-recovered event for that index.
lessons.refute_if: Every such entry is preceded by a logged chain recovery, or none occur.

lessons.claim: All three trades were entered one minute after a same-setup rejection with EV within ±0.04R. Examples: ORB rejected at 09:35/09:36, entered 09:37; trend_break rejected at 12:00/12:01, entered 12:02. The clearing EV is never logged.
lessons.why: Entries flicker across the EV floor on noise rather than any real edge. Every such entry lost today, and the same pattern recurred on earlier days.
lessons.uncertainty: Only three trades. The EV at entry is unknown, and the near-floor EV may simply be the normal state for these setups.
lessons.hypothesis: Entries preceded within 3 min by a same-setup rejection with |EV| ≤ 0.04R realize lower mean R than entries without such a preceding rejection.
lessons.confirm_if: Over 28+ sessions, the mean R of flicker-entries is below the mean R of other entries, with a non-overlapping bootstrap interval.
lessons.refute_if: Mean R is equal or higher for flicker-entries over that sample.

lessons.claim: The ORB entered at +2.1σ above VWAP on relative volume 0.81, with invalidation at VWAP 22,953.93, about 32 pts below the 22,986 entry. It reached 0.52R of open profit and then exited at -0.74R. NIFTY went on to 23,097 by noon.
lessons.why: A sub-1.0 relative-volume break, entered stretched far above VWAP with a stop at VWAP, invited a mean-reversion stop-out. The day's direction (up) was right.
lessons.uncertainty: One trade. The later rally may be unrelated. A wider stop would have needed smaller size, and the 10:33 low near 22,916 would also have tested it.
lessons.hypothesis: ORB entries with relative volume <1.0 and >1.5σ above VWAP hit invalidation more often than other ORB entries.
lessons.confirm_if: Over 28+ sessions, the invalidation-exit rate for that subgroup exceeds the rest by ≥15 points.
lessons.refute_if: The invalidation rate is similar or lower for that subgroup.

lessons.claim: The 45-minute no-progress time exits held the 12:02 trend_break losses to -0.07R and -0.20R. Best open profit was 0.19R and 0.04R, and worst heat was 0.44R and 0.38R.
lessons.why: Both breakouts stalled immediately. Cutting at 45 minutes stopped worst heat of about 0.4R from becoming a full loss.
lessons.uncertainty: Bars after 12:47 are not given, so the trades may have recovered later. On earlier days, time exits gave up open profit.

lessons.claim: The BANKNIFTY iron_fly was re-priced every minute from 11:00 to 11:09 with EV pinned at -0.03R to -0.04R while P(profit) swung between 14% and 29%. That is implausible for a short fly on a balance day.
lessons.why: Pricing came from the NSE fallback while the kotak chain was down. The P(profit) model may be broken, which would make range_sell rejections uninformative.
lessons.uncertainty: The fly could be genuinely costly in a fast BANKNIFTY. This may be unrelated to the fallback data source.
lessons.hypothesis: Iron_fly P(profit) estimates are lower and noisier when the chain is on the NSE fallback than when the kotak chain is live.
lessons.confirm_if: Across sessions, median iron_fly P(profit) is at least 15 points lower under fallback, at similar range-day conditions.
lessons.refute_if: P(profit) distributions are similar between fallback and live-chain periods.
